newsitem.title: USA: Corvas drug shows anticoagulant ability.
newsitem.headline: Corvas drug shows anticoagulant ability.

text.p: Corvas International Inc said on Wednesday that preclinical studies showed that its NAPc2 drug shows significant anticoagulant properties.
Corvas plans human trials with this compound, which is believed to block blood clot formations, in early 1997 to treat deep vein thrombosis, Corvas said.

Corvas published the three abstracts presented in the October issue of Circulation, a journal of the American Heart Association, on data pertaining to preclinical studies of the compound that comes from the blood-feeding hookworm Ancylostoma caninum.

Corvas said a test of a recombinant form of NAPc2 in pigs showed that intravenous administration of the agent prevented acute platelet dependent arterial thrombosis in coronary arteries without any side effects.

In a rat model of thrombosis, recombinant NAPc2 demonstrated significant antithrombotic efficacy and potential safety advantages over a version of heparin following either intravenous or subcutaneous administration at doses that did not result in an increase in surgical bleeding.
